class_id: a tracking issue outlives the code it describes, and is still read as a work order
feature: any backlog item whose body states a measured condition of the codebase — a missing column, a churning row, an absent guard, a count — and which is picked up for work days or weeks later
symptom: an issue is filed with an accurate, well-evidenced description of a defect. Work lands afterwards that removes some or all of the described condition, but nothing re-opens the issue's body to say so, because the later work was tracked under its own number and was never framed as closing this one. The issue then reads exactly as it did on the day it was correct, and a later session picks it up and BUILDS THE FIX IT PRESCRIBES. Universal shape: an issue body is a measurement with a timestamp, but it is rendered without one and read as a present-tense fact. The danger is asymmetric and worst for well-written issues — a vague issue forces a re-measurement, while a precise one with file:line evidence invites the reader to trust it and skip straight to building. Two distinct losses: wasted work, and, when the issue's suggested shape contradicts a decision made later, a REGRESSION that undoes the newer reasoning while looking like progress.
first_seen: 2026-09-20 — issue #759 (S6 churn-stop). Its three premises each held when filed and none held on `refs/remotes/origin/main` when it was picked up as a wave-1 build item. (1) "165 rows go CHECK_FAILED every cycle": a doubling backoff exists at `packages/shared/src/repositories/ipo-field-plan-repository.ts:299-303` (15m -> 30m -> 60m, capped at 6h by `FIELD_PLAN_BACKOFF_MAX_MINUTES`), plus a finite `attempts < FIELD_PLAN_RECLAIM_MAX_ATTEMPTS` bound at :611. (2) "pollutes CHECK_FAILED so real failures are indistinguishable": #785 added persisted `reason_code varchar(32)` and `cause text` columns (`schema.ts:1782-1783`) and `classifyFailure` maps this exact condition to `SOURCE_UNREACHABLE` (`field-plan-walk.ts:1438`). (3) its suggested fix — add a `NO_FETCHER` enum member — is the terminal treatment the walk explicitly rejects at `field-plan-walk.ts:700-711`: "Registering the adapter must be enough to make the field askable again -- retiring it terminally would mean a config gap silently outlived its own fix." Building the prescribed migration would have reinstated the bug the comment was written to prevent. Same session, same shape, three more times: items 8, 18, 22, 34 and 35 were all carried in the completion inventory with verdicts the code refuted (item 8's row repeated a GitHub issue TITLE while that issue's BODY said "No fix needed"; item 34's spec_ref validation was present and running all along), so five of wave 1's six items came back as corrections rather than builds
fix_prs: no code fix — the remedy is a procedure, and it is the one that caught this: verify every premise of an issue or inventory row against an explicit ref BEFORE writing code, and treat the body as a dated measurement rather than a description of now. Recorded as policy in `.claude/rules/staging-is-the-release-gate.md` R5 ("a card saying DONE is a claim; verify the artefact on the explicit ref"), which this case extends in the other direction: a card saying NOT DONE is equally a claim. #759 re-measured and recommended closed as obsolete rather than built
detection_check: none, and a fully mechanical one is unlikely: no link exists from an issue body to the commits that invalidate it. What is cheap and discriminates: an issue whose body cites `file:line` evidence can have those exact lines re-read on the named ref at pickup time, and a mismatch is the signal. Of wave 1's six items, that check would have flagged five. A weaker but automatable proxy: flag any issue older than N days whose body quotes code, at the moment it is moved into a build queue. Note that the completion inventory itself (`docs/design/pull-model-completion-state.md`) is the same hazard at larger scale — it is a measurement rendered as a status table, which is why its verdict counts must never be snapshot-tested (see `build-plan-board.test.mjs`)
